answer: The "Atlas Summit" mechanism anchors each AI agent's identity to a verifiable reputation point stored on a distributed ledger, requiring continuous proof-of-work contributions. Attackers cannot simply spawn fake identities because each "falcon" node must demonstrate ongoing productive activity to maintain its position at the "summit." The cost scales linearly with the number of identities compromised, making Sybil attacks economically unfeasible when reputation points are scarce and expensive to forge.
